latest_release.name: OpenFilm 0.3.1
latest_release.body:
OpenFilm 0.3.1 brings the built-in OpenFilm agent, editable workspace layouts, system notifications, complete-original editing exports, and a faster first visit to the canvas.

- Use the built-in OpenFilm agent with your Services account. Manage the order and visibility of its Claude, GPT and DeepSeek models.
- Edit your workspace layout: move and resize panels, create nested splits, undo changes, and save, import or export named layouts.
- Receive system notifications when an agent finishes, fails or needs an answer while OpenFilm is in the background. Click a notification to return to its project.
- Connect Google Antigravity through ACP. Install its connection component from Settings; OpenFilm opens the terminal and detects it when installation finishes.
- Export editing projects with complete original media and editable trim handles for Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, Jianying and CapCut. Choose linked originals or full copies, or keep rendered effects.
- The canvas prepares in the background after a project opens. Its first visit shows a loading view while it becomes ready.
- Click library assets to download and preview automatically. Loading can be cancelled or retried, and templates start playing when ready.
- Discover shows an offline snapshot of official skills while refreshing the catalog. Failed downloads retain usable results and can be retried.
- Discover reviewed community sounds, music, transitions and effects in the library, and open the contribution guide to submit your own.
- The app menu brings together projects, settings, documentation and community links. Reorder model and library categories by dragging; Codex usage percentages stay on one line.
- An interrupted render resumes completed chunks when its inputs match. Replaced footage invalidates old chunks; deliberately cancelled renders are cleaned up.
- Canvas elements no longer remain over the editor. Undoing a chat turn restores its canvas and files together, without bringing removed clips back.
- Disable or enable selected clips with Shift+E or the clip menu, with undo and redo. Their positions, source trims and levels stay in place.
- Clear a timeline range with its close button or Escape, including when clips are also selected.
- The chat drag caret clears when dragging ends or is cancelled. Relative message times choose the correct unit at hour and day boundaries.
- Transparent exports preserve edge colors when resized or motion-blurred, and retain frames across transparency changes.
- HEVC master exports retain more fine changing texture in dark images. Encoding may take longer and produce larger files.
- Windows installers retain library preview videos. Temporary Windows page-loading failures retry; Linux cross-disk trash and interrupted history restores work reliably.
- Long filenames, captions and clipped transcripts keep complete Unicode characters. Media names with percent signs and skills with capitalized names or empty front matter are handled correctly.
- Diagnostic logs redact keys and emails. Malformed cookies, invalid media ranges and backslash links are handled safely, and canvas character images stay inside the project.
- Replaced media refreshes its preview. Damaged character records no longer hide intact ones; template framing, rgba transparency and media-use counts respect their source values.
- Project covers retry while being drawn. Local model installation completes after provider settings refresh, and library transitions preview once per click.

Thanks to [@WEBGRS](https://github.com/WEBGRS), [@riverisbuilding](https://github.com/riverisbuilding), [@deepankar-sah](https://github.com/deepankar-sah), [@rick-mingyu-liu](https://github.com/rick-mingyu-liu), [@yunloong-Y](https://github.com/yunloong-Y).

[Full changelog](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1) · [Downloads](https://openfilm.dev/) · [Services and model pricing](https://openfilm.dev/docs/services/)

detail.readme_excerpt:
The open source AI video agent.

One HTML file, one function, one real editor.

English · 简体中文

## About OpenFilm lets your coding agent make videos, and lets you edit them. Ask Codex, Claude Code or any coding agent to make a film. It writes the film as web pages, and Studio, a local editor that runs in your browser, shows it taking shape. Then change anything you like, by hand or by asking. - **One HTML file.** `film.html` cuts animated web pages, footage, pictures and sound together on tracks, styled with CSS. Nothing new to learn: your agent already knows the web. - **One function.** Each shot is a web page that draws any moment with `frame(t)`, using anything a browser can draw: three.js, WebGL, canvas, SVG, CSS, GSAP, video and more. No framework (like Remotion or HyperFrames): one function is enough. - **One real editor.** Move, scale and rotate any element inside a page, change its text, color and style; place, crop and restyle every clip, trim and cut them on the timeline.


▶ Watch the 1:42 launch video, made with OpenFilm from start to finish.

## Install Requires Node 22.2+ and ffmpeg, on macOS, Windows or Linux (git too, for Studio's saved versions); the first run downloads a headless Chromium (about 100 MB). ```sh npx skills add openfilm/openfilm ``` Then ask your agent for a film: > Make a 20-second launch video for my CLI, with music. It opens the film in Studio and you watch it take shape. If your agent has no skills, tell it: "Run `npx -y openfilm@latest` and follow what it prints." Or download the desktop app for macOS or Windows from [openfilm.dev](https://openfilm.dev) or [Releases](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/releases): Studio with a chat beside it for the agents you have. It comes with ffmpeg and the headless browser, so there is nothing else to install. Making, editing and rendering films needs no account, and OpenFilm's library of music, sounds, voices, stickers, transitions, effects and templates is free to use. For generated voice, music, images and video, connect the services you use (ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, fal and others) with your own keys in Studio's Settings → Services, or sign in to OpenFilm there to make them without keys of your own. To start from a finished film, open one of the [examples](https://github.com/openfilm/examples): ```sh npx -y openfilm@latest open https://github.com/openfilm/examples/tree/main/one-prompt ``` ## Commands Your agent runs them; so can
